title: OHCHR Indigenous Fellowship Programme 2027: Fully Funded UN Human Rights Fellowship in Geneva
summary: The Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) is now accepting applications for the Indigenous Fellowship Programme 2027 . This prestigious, fully funded fellowship offers indigenous leaders from around the world an opportunity to strengthen their knowledge of the United Nations human rights system and gain practical skills to advance and protect the rights of indigenous peoples. The programme brings together fellows from different regions and language backgrounds for an intensive four-week training in Geneva, Switzerland , while providing a unique opportunity to engage directly with UN human rights mechanisms. Key Summary Host: Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) Programme: Indigenous Fellowship Programme 2027 Location: Geneva, Switzerland Duration: 4 weeks (June/July 2027) Funding: Fully funded (return airfare, living expenses, and basic health insurance) Languages: English, French, Spanish, and Portuguese Eligibility: Indigenous persons nominated by an indigenous organization or community Education Requirement: No formal educational qualifications required Application Deadline: 6 September 2026 (23:59 Geneva time) Application Method: Online application with a recommendation letter from the nominating indigenous organization or community General information: The Indigenous Fellowship Programme was launched in 1997 by the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) in the context of the first International Decade of the World s Indigenous People. The aim of the programme is to give indigenous persons the opportunity to gain knowledge about the UN system and mechanisms dealing with human rights issues in general and indigenous issues in particular. Trained participants are better equipped to assist their organisations and communities in protecting and promoting their rights. This training programme is available in 4 languages: English , Spanish , French and Portuguese . When does it take place? Fellows from all 4 language components of the programme are trained together with simultaneous interpretation over 4 weeks in Geneva . The date of the training programme usually coincides with the annual session of the Expert Mechanism on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples ( June/July each year), allowing the fellows to participate more actively in that Mechanism. What does the programme cover? The selected candidates are entitled to a return flight ticket, living expenses and basic health insurance for the duration of the training. Who can apply for the programme? The candidate must be indigenous (non-indigenous persons will not be taken into consideration, even if they have close links with indigenous communities and/or organizations). Indigenous candidates, including women, LGBTQI+ individuals, and persons with disabilities, are strongly encouraged to apply. Age should not be a limitation to participation in the programme. Formal education should not be a limitation to participation in the IFP given the socio-economic barriers confronted by many indigenous peoples that limit access to formal educational institutions. Candidates should agree to train other indigenous persons after the return to their respective communities/organizations. The candidate should be proposed, and his/her candidacy supported by his/her indigenous organization and/or community. It is desirable that the sponsoring organization has a firm constituency or membership and that it is representative. The candidate should have a good working knowledge of the language in which the programme is imparted. Application procedure: We strongly encourage you to submit you online application well before the deadline of 6 September 2026 (23:59 Geneva time) . Fellowship applications will only be taken into consideration if they are fully completed. Both parts I and II of the application form must be completed Application forms must include an official recommendation letter from the nominating Indigenous organization or community. Applicants should upload their recommendation letters directly to the online application form. The application form is available at: https://survey.ohchr.org/429282?lang=en Selection process: The selection of fellows reflects a gender and regional balance, as well as a balance between communities represented. The general human rights situation in the respective regions/countries is also taken into consideration. A pre-selection of 15 to 20 candidates per language group is made by previous indigenous fellows. The selection process also entails interviews of pre-selected candidates who applied to either the English, French, Spanish or Portuguese language components of the programme. The final selection of successful candidates is reviewed by an advisory group composed of OHCHR staff. In view of the large number of applications, ONLY PRE-SELECTED CANDIDATES ARE CONTACTED. Any other questions? Any question pertaining to the Indigenous Fellowship Programme can be e-mailed to: ohchr-fellowship@un.org . title: Ghana2Germany Initiative Opens Applications for Lifeguard Training and Germany Apprenticeship Pathway for Young Ghanaians
summary: Young Ghanaians seeking to build internationally recognized skills while preparing for future apprenticeship opportunities in Germany now have an exciting opportunity through the ghana2germany initiative . Implemented by the Delegation of German Industry and Commerce in Ghana (AHK Ghana) in collaboration with GIZ Ghana through the Ghanaian European Centre for Migration (GEC) , the initiative is designed to strengthen technical and vocational skills, improve employability, and create pathways to international careers. As part of this initiative, the programme has partnered with the Ghana Lifesaving and Diving Association (GHALDA) to provide specialized training in swimming, lifesaving, and water safety for young people in Kumasi. Successful applicants will receive comprehensive professional training leading to nationally and internationally recognized lifeguard certifications, German language instruction, and the opportunity to pursue dual apprenticeship training in Germany. The programme represents an important investment in youth development by combining technical skills, language training, and international career preparation into one structured pathway. About the Ghana2Germany Initiative The ghana2germany initiative is a Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) support programme established to improve the quality of vocational education while preparing young people for employment opportunities in Ghana and Germany. The programme focuses on strengthening technical competencies, improving soft skills, and enhancing vocational training institutions so that graduates possess industry-relevant knowledge and practical experience. Beyond improving training institutions, the initiative seeks to create a highly skilled workforce capable of meeting labour market demands in both Ghana and Germany through internationally aligned vocational education and apprenticeship opportunities. Partnership Behind the Programme The programme is implemented through collaboration among several organizations committed to youth development and international vocational training. These include: Delegation of German Industry and Commerce in Ghana (AHK Ghana) GIZ Ghana Ghanaian European Centre for Migration (GEC) Ghana Lifesaving and Diving Association (GHALDA) Together, these organizations combine expertise in vocational education, migration support, technical skills development, and international cooperation to deliver a comprehensive training programme. Purpose of the Programme The ghana2germany initiative aims to prepare young Ghanaians for meaningful employment by providing practical vocational education that aligns with current industry needs. Its objectives include: Strengthening technical skills. Developing soft skills required in modern workplaces. Improving TVET workshop facilities. Enhancing vocational education quality. Building industry-relevant competencies. Preparing participants for dual apprenticeship opportunities. Supporting labour mobility between Ghana and Germany. Creating a highly qualified workforce. Expanding international employment opportunities. Promoting safe swimming and lifesaving practices. Specialized Lifeguard Training Programme As part of this initiative, a dedicated lifeguard training programme has been introduced in partnership with GHALDA. The programme aims to provide participants with advanced practical training in: Swimming Lifesaving Water rescue Water safety Emergency response Participants will develop professional competencies required for lifeguard responsibilities while meeting recognized certification standards. Number of Participants The programme will pre-select fifteen (15) young Ghanaians to participate in the comprehensive training programme. Only shortlisted candidates will progress through the selection process following evaluation against the programme s internal eligibility criteria. Training Components Successful participants will receive extensive professional development covering multiple areas. 1. Professional Swimming Training Participants will improve their swimming skills through structured instruction designed to prepare them for professional lifesaving responsibilities. Training may include: Swimming techniques Endurance development Water confidence Rescue swimming Practical assessments 2. Lifesaving Skills Training Participants will receive specialized instruction in professional lifesaving techniques. Areas of focus include: Rescue procedures Emergency response Victim assistance Water rescue operations Public safety 3. Water Safety Education Understanding water safety is an essential part of professional lifeguarding. Training includes: Risk identification Accident prevention Public awareness Safe swimming practices Hazard management 4. National Lifeguard Certification Participants who successfully complete the programme will work toward obtaining a National Lifeguard Certification/License , demonstrating their competence according to national standards. 5. International Lifeguard License Beyond national certification, trainees will also have the opportunity to earn an International Lifeguard License , enhancing their professional credentials and improving employability internationally. 6. German Language Training Language preparation forms an important component of the programme. Selected participants will receive German language instruction covering: A1 Level A2 Level Developing language skills prepares participants for future apprenticeship and work opportunities in Germany. Opportunity for Dual Apprenticeship Training in Germany One of the programme s most significant features is the opportunity for selected participants to travel to Germany for dual apprenticeship training . Germany s dual apprenticeship model combines classroom instruction with practical workplace experience, allowing participants to build technical expertise while gaining hands-on industry experience. Participation in this pathway may significantly improve future employment prospects. However, applicants should note that submission of an application does not guarantee placement, employment, sponsorship, or relocation. Long-Term Career Prospects The initiative seeks to prepare participants for future opportunities by equipping them with internationally relevant skills. Potential long-term outcomes include: Improved employability International vocational experience Professional certification Enhanced technical competencies Language proficiency Greater competitiveness in the labour market Access to apprenticeship opportunities in Germany Application Process Interested applicants are required to complete the official application form carefully and provide accurate information throughout the process. Applicants are advised to: Complete every section carefully. Provide truthful information. Ensure all personal details are accurate. Submit complete responses. Incomplete or misleading information may negatively affect the application. Information Required During Application Applicants will be asked to provide information including: Personal Information Full name Date of birth Nationality Gender City or region of residence Residential address Phone number Email address Educational Background Applicants must indicate: Highest educational qualification obtained Name of educational institution Educational options include: JHS SHS TVET Institution Diploma Degree Swimming Experience Applicants will provide information regarding: Ability to swim without assistance Swimming proficiency level Previous formal swimming training Swimming ability categories include: Beginner Intermediate Advanced Competitive Swimmer Previous Training Applicants may indicate previous participation in: Lifeguard Training Swimming Instructor Training Water Safety Programmes Diving Training Rescue Swimming Training Applicants with no previous experience may also apply. Professional Certifications Applicants will indicate whether they currently hold certifications related to: Swimming Lifesaving First Aid CPR Emergency Response If applicable, applicants should provide details. Motivation Questions Applicants are also required to answer written questions covering: Why they wish to become certified lifeguards. Personal qualities that make them suitable for the programme. Examples demonstrating leadership, responsibility, or emergency response. These responses help assess motivation and suitability beyond technical qualifications. Selection Process Submitting an application does not guarantee : Selection Participation Employment Sponsorship Placement Apprenticeship Visa support Future work opportunities Applications will be evaluated according to internally established eligibility criteria. Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted. Selected candidates can expect an email invitation for interviews approximately one week after submitting their application. Applicant Declaration Applicants must confirm that: Information provided is accurate. False information may result in disqualification. Participation in selection does not guarantee programme admission. They understand certification and employment are not guaranteed. Applicants must also provide their signature by entering their full name in capital letters. Health and Participation Requirements Applicants confirm that they: Are physically fit for intensive swimming and rescue training. Do not have medical conditions affecting participation. Are willing to learn German. Are willing to relocate to Germany if future apprenticeship or employment opportunities become available. These declarations ensure participants are prepared for the demands of the programme. Important Disclaimer The programme emphasizes that applicants who are not contacted should consider their application unsuccessful for the current intake. However, unsuccessful applicants are encouraged to remain optimistic, as future opportunities under the ghana2germany initiative may become available. Visit here for more details on Ghana2Germany Initiative Opens Applications for Lifeguard Training and Germany Apprenticeship Application Deadline No application deadline has been specified in the available information. Interested applicants are encouraged to complete and submit their application as early as possible before the selection process advances. Apply here Why This Programme Stands Out The ghana2germany initiative offers far more than technical training. By combining internationally recognized lifeguard certification, German language education, vocational development, and the possibility of participating in Germany s dual apprenticeship system, the programme creates a unique pathway for young Ghanaians to develop valuable skills and broaden their career prospects. Its integrated approach supports both personal and professional development while strengthening the connection between vocational education in Ghana and international labour market opportunities. Conclusion The ghana2germany initiative represents a significant opportunity for young Ghanaians interested in developing professional skills in swimming, lifesaving, and water safety while preparing for potential apprenticeship opportunities in Germany. Through collaboration between AHK Ghana, GIZ Ghana, the Ghanaian European Centre for Migration, and the Ghana Lifesaving and Diving Association, the programme delivers high-quality vocational training, internationally recognized certifications, German language instruction, and exposure to Germany s dual apprenticeship model. Although selection is competitive and participation does not guarantee employment or relocation, the initiative provides participants with valuable technical competencies, leadership experience, and internationally relevant qualifications that can strengthen their long-term career prospects. Eligible young Ghanaians who are motivated, physically fit, and committed to professional development are encouraged to submit a complete and accurate application for this unique training opportunity. title: GAUC Climate x Leadership Training Program 2025: Empowering the Next Generation of Global Climate Leaders for a Carbon-Neutral Future
summary: Climate change remains one of the defining challenges of the 21st century, affecting economies, ecosystems, communities, and future generations across the globe. As countries accelerate efforts to achieve carbon neutrality and sustainable development, there is an increasing need for young leaders equipped with the knowledge, leadership skills, and interdisciplinary understanding required to drive meaningful climate action. Recognizing this urgent need, the Global Alliance of Universities on Climate (GAUC) has launched the 2025 Climate x Leadership Training Program , an international learning initiative designed to prepare young people to become leaders in the global transition toward a carbon-neutral future. The program seeks to empower youth by providing them with comprehensive knowledge, practical tools, and leadership capabilities that enable them to understand climate challenges, explore innovative solutions, and contribute to sustainable development at local, national, and international levels. Built around the concept of interdisciplinary climate leadership, the Climate x Leadership Training Program encourages participants to look beyond traditional environmental approaches and understand how climate action connects with every aspect of sustainable development. About the Climate x Leadership Training Program The Climate x Leadership Training Program is an educational initiative developed by the Global Alliance of Universities on Climate (GAUC) to prepare future leaders capable of addressing the complex challenges posed by climate change. Rather than focusing solely on environmental science, the program adopts a multidisciplinary perspective, recognizing that climate change intersects with economics, governance, agriculture, food systems, resilience, public policy, innovation, and sustainable development. Participants are introduced to the knowledge, perspectives, and leadership competencies needed to contribute effectively to global climate solutions while understanding the interconnected nature of today s development challenges. The program emphasizes that achieving carbon neutrality requires a comprehensive transformation of societies, economies, and institutions rather than simply replacing fossil fuels with renewable energy sources. Program Vision The Climate x Leadership Training Program is built around the vision of creating a new generation of globally minded climate leaders who can support the transition toward sustainable and carbon-neutral development. According to GAUC, transitioning to a carbon-neutral economy represents far more than an energy transition. It involves: Transforming economic systems Rethinking development models Promoting sustainable modernization Protecting natural ecosystems Encouraging innovation Supporting inclusive economic growth Building resilient societies Creating a greener and more prosperous future Through this program, participants are encouraged to understand climate action within this broader global context. Program Objectives The Climate x Leadership Training Program seeks to achieve several important objectives. These include: Empowering youth with climate knowledge Developing future climate leaders Building interdisciplinary understanding Promoting sustainable development Encouraging innovation Supporting carbon neutrality goals Strengthening leadership capacity Inspiring meaningful climate action Equipping participants with practical tools Developing global perspectives on sustainability Ultimately, the program aims to prepare participants to become active contributors to climate solutions within their communities, institutions, and countries. Why the Climate x Initiative Matters Climate challenges cannot be solved through isolated actions. The Climate x initiative emphasizes that today s global issues are deeply interconnected. Environmental sustainability is linked with: Economic development Food security Public health Education Social inclusion Governance Innovation Infrastructure Energy systems Global cooperation By recognizing these relationships, the program encourages participants to develop integrated solutions capable of generating positive outcomes across multiple sectors. Climate Action and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) One of the central ideas behind the Climate x Leadership Training Program is that climate action should be pursued alongside the broader United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) . Rather than treating climate change as a separate issue, the program encourages participants to understand how climate solutions contribute to progress across the remaining SDGs. This integrated approach supports: Sustainable economic growth Poverty reduction Food security Environmental protection Clean energy Responsible consumption Innovation Strong institutions Global partnerships The program highlights the importance of creating synergies between climate action and sustainable development. A Vision from Global Climate Leadership The Climate x Leadership Training Program features insights from Lord Nicholas Stern , Chair of GAUC s Academic Committee and Chair of the Grantham Research Institute on Climate Change and the Environment at the London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE) . The initiative reflects the belief that young people are not merely inheritors of the future but also its creators, owners, and leaders. The program emphasizes that empowering youth with the right knowledge and leadership skills is essential for achieving a successful transition to a net-zero future. Program Structure The Climate x Leadership Training Program includes an intensive one-month knowledge immersion experience designed to provide participants with both foundational understanding and practical perspectives on climate leadership. During the program, learners engage with key themes that shape global climate action and sustainable development. Learning Areas The curriculum is organized around several important subject areas. 1. Climate x Adaptation Resilience Participants explore strategies for helping societies adapt to climate change while strengthening resilience against environmental, economic, and social risks. Topics may include: Climate adaptation Disaster resilience Community resilience Risk reduction Sustainable planning Long-term climate preparedness 2. Climate x Food Food systems play a critical role in both contributing to and addressing climate change. This module introduces participants to issues such as: Sustainable agriculture Food security Climate-smart farming Environmental sustainability Agricultural innovation Resilient food systems 3. Global Climate Governance Climate action depends upon cooperation among governments, international organizations, institutions, businesses, and communities. Participants gain insight into: International climate agreements Global cooperation Climate diplomacy Climate policy International institutions Governance frameworks 4. Youth Leadership Developing leadership capacity is a central focus of the program. Participants strengthen skills including: Leadership Communication Collaboration Strategic thinking Problem-solving Global citizenship Change management Innovation Why Youth Are Central to the Program GAUC recognizes young people as essential partners in building a carbon-neutral future. The program highlights that youth are: Future leaders Current innovators Decision-makers of tomorrow Contributors to sustainable development Drivers of climate action Agents of positive change By investing in youth leadership today, the program aims to support long-term global sustainability. Benefits of Participating Although the available information does not list formal participant benefits, learners can expect opportunities to: Build knowledge of climate change and sustainability Strengthen leadership skills Understand carbon neutrality Explore interdisciplinary climate solutions Learn from an internationally focused curriculum Develop a broader understanding of global climate governance Enhance professional and academic knowledge Join a community interested in climate leadership Visit here for more details on GAUC Climate x Leadership Training Program 2025 About the Global Alliance of Universities on Climate (GAUC) The Global Alliance of Universities on Climate (GAUC) is an international network dedicated to advancing climate education, research, collaboration, and leadership. Through educational initiatives such as the Climate x Leadership Training Program, GAUC seeks to mobilize universities, researchers, students, and young professionals to contribute toward global climate solutions and sustainable development. The alliance promotes interdisciplinary learning and international cooperation to help prepare future leaders capable of addressing complex environmental challenges. Registration and Updates Individuals interested in the Climate x Leadership Training Program can register their interest through the official GAUC platform. Prospective participants may choose to: Receive reminders when admissions begin. Subscribe to the GAUC Newsletter for updates on future programs, climate education initiatives, and related opportunities. Apply here Application Deadline No application deadline has been announced in the available information. Interested participants are encouraged to register their interest through the official GAUC website and subscribe for admission notifications. Why This Program Is Worth Considering The Climate x Leadership Training Program offers an opportunity for young people to build a strong foundation in climate leadership while exploring how climate action intersects with global development. Its interdisciplinary approach encourages participants to think beyond traditional environmental solutions and develop a broader understanding of sustainability, governance, innovation, and resilience. As governments, businesses, and organizations increasingly prioritize climate action and carbon neutrality, individuals with knowledge of climate leadership and sustainable development will be well positioned to contribute meaningfully across a wide range of sectors. Conclusion The GAUC Climate x Leadership Training Program 2025 is an important global initiative designed to prepare young leaders for the challenges and opportunities of a carbon-neutral future. By combining interdisciplinary learning with leadership development, the program equips participants to understand the complex relationships between climate change, sustainable development, governance, resilience, and innovation. Open to youth worldwide, the one-month knowledge immersion experience encourages participants to become active contributors to global climate solutions while developing the skills needed to lead positive environmental and societal change. For students, emerging professionals, and aspiring climate leaders seeking to expand their understanding of sustainability and leadership, the Climate x Leadership Training Program offers a valuable opportunity to engage with one of the most significant global issues of our time. title: UNDP & ISS Call for Papers 2026: Submit Your Research on Youth-Safe Digital Futures in Africa
summary: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) , in partnership with the Institute for Security Studies (ISS) , has officially launched the Call for Papers: Youth-Safe Digital Futures , inviting researchers, practitioners, youth experts, digital rights advocates, and technology policy specialists from across Africa to contribute to an important new policy compendium focused on creating safer, more inclusive digital environments for young people. The forthcoming publication, titled Youth-Safe Digital Futures: From Digital Inclusion to Responsible AI for Peace and Development in Africa, seeks high-quality analytical papers that explore how Africa can build digital ecosystems where young people can safely access opportunities, participate in governance, innovate, and benefit from emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI). As digital transformation accelerates across Africa, this initiative recognizes that providing internet access alone is no longer enough. Instead, the focus is shifting toward ensuring that digital technologies promote peace, inclusion, accountability, innovation, and sustainable development while protecting young people from online risks and harms. Researchers and practitioners with expertise in digital governance, AI, youth development, peacebuilding, cybersecurity, media, and public policy are encouraged to submit original policy papers before the application deadline. About the Youth-Safe Digital Futures Compendium Young Africans are increasingly using digital platforms to: Access education. Build sustainable livelihoods. Launch startups and social enterprises. Participate in civic engagement. Advocate for policy change. Contribute to democratic processes. Engage in entrepreneurship and innovation. However, rapid digital transformation has also introduced numerous challenges. Young people frequently encounter: Online harassment. Cyber scams and fraud. Surveillance. Algorithmic discrimination. Digital exclusion. Online misinformation and disinformation. Manipulated digital content. Technology-facilitated violence. Limited representation of African languages and local realities in AI systems. Recognizing these challenges, the UNDP and ISS are developing a policy compendium that moves beyond digital access toward creating youth-safe digital futures , where young people can participate confidently, safely, and meaningfully in digital and AI-enabled societies. Purpose of the Compendium The publication seeks to answer several critical policy questions, including: How can African youth access and benefit from AI-enabled transformation? What governance mechanisms are needed to minimize AI-related risks? How can digital trust be strengthened to promote peace and social cohesion? How can AI contribute positively to sustainable development? Who benefits from AI-driven innovation? How can digital systems become more inclusive, equitable, and accountable? The publication aligns with major regional and global policy frameworks, including: African Union Digital Transformation Strategy for Africa (2020–2030) African Union Continental Artificial Intelligence Strategy Global Digital Compact UNDP Digital and Artificial Intelligence Strategy Scope of the Publication The compendium will include: 8–10 thematic policy papers 3–4 African case studies A comprehensive synthesis chapter outlining a policy agenda for youth-safe digital futures across Africa Contributors are expected to provide analytical and evidence-based papers rather than descriptive summaries. Papers should connect local experiences with national, regional, and continental policy discussions while drawing primarily on African evidence and experiences. Thematic Areas Authors should submit papers addressing one of the following four themes. Theme 1: Digital and AI Inclusion for Peace and Development Topics may include: Digital inclusion Affordable internet access AI literacy Digital literacy Rural and urban digital inequalities Gender gaps in digital access Disability inclusion Local language technologies Online safety Algorithmic bias Digital exclusion Theme 2: Safe Digital Spaces, Rights and Protection Possible topics include: Cyberbullying Online harassment Technology-facilitated gender-based violence Digital scams Online exploitation Extremist recruitment Privacy and surveillance Mental health and digital wellbeing Digital rights Child and youth online protection Theme 3: Information Integrity, Media and Social Cohesion Authors may explore: Misinformation Disinformation Hate speech Election-related misinformation Digital trust Social media governance Civic participation Fact-checking Digital media Peacebuilding through information integrity Theme 4: Youth Innovation, Digital Livelihoods and Resilience Suggested areas include: Artificial Intelligence innovation Youth entrepreneurship Digital startups Creative industries Climate technology Civic technology Community resilience Peacebuilding innovation Financing digital innovation Public-private partnerships Who Should Submit Papers? The organizers welcome submissions from individuals and organizations with expertise in relevant fields. Eligible contributors include: Researchers Academics Youth experts Civil society organizations Technology policy specialists Digital rights advocates Peacebuilding practitioners Think tanks Development professionals Youth-led organizations Editorial Requirements Submitted papers must: Be approximately 2,000 words . Present original analysis. Be intellectually authored by humans. Not be simultaneously submitted elsewhere. Successfully pass plagiarism screening. Undergo editorial review. Undergo external peer review. While AI-assisted tools may be used for editing, transcription, coding, translation, or literature organization, authors must disclose such use. AI-generated papers will not be accepted. Required Paper Structure Each submission should include: Executive summary or abstract. Problem statement. Definitions of key concepts. Methodology section. Evidence-based analysis. Gender considerations. Youth inclusion considerations. Disability inclusion considerations. Conflict-sensitive analysis. Policy recommendations at: Community level National level Regional level Continental level Complete reference list using: APA 7th Edition, or Chicago Author-Date referencing style Submission Process Authors should submit their completed 2,000-word paper by email. Submissions should be sent to: Raquel Leandro – raquel.leandro@undp.org Christella Igiraneza – christella.igiraneza@undp.org Emmaculate Liaga – eliaga@issafrica.org Important Dates Activity Date Call for Papers Opens 23 July 2026 Submission Deadline 31 August 2026 Internal Review End of September 2026 External Peer Review Mid-October 2026 Editing and Finalization Mid-November – December 2026 For More Information To learn more about the Youth-Safe Digital Futures Call for Papers , including submission requirements, thematic guidance, editorial expectations, and the complete announcement, applicants should visit the official UNDP Africa webpage HERE Prospective contributors are encouraged to review the official guidance carefully before preparing and submitting their papers to ensure they meet all editorial and submission requirements. Why You Should Apply This Call for Papers provides a valuable opportunity to contribute to one of Africa s most important policy discussions on digital transformation, artificial intelligence, youth participation, and peacebuilding. Selected contributors will help shape evidence-based recommendations that can influence digital governance, AI policy, and youth-focused development across the continent. Whether you are a researcher, policymaker, practitioner, or digital rights advocate, your work can contribute to building a future where Africa s young people not only access digital technologies but also use them safely, equitably, and meaningfully. Conclusion The UNDP and ISS Youth-Safe Digital Futures Call for Papers 2026 offers an important platform for African experts to contribute original research and policy analysis on the future of digital inclusion, AI governance, online safety, and youth empowerment. By bringing together evidence from across the continent, this compendium aims to inform policies that strengthen peace, digital rights, innovation, and inclusive development. Interested contributors should begin preparing their original analytical papers early and submit them no later than 31 August 2026 to be considered for inclusion in this landmark publication. title: 2026 African Plant Nutrition Outreach Fellowship: Win a USD $5,000 Fellowship to Advance Sustainable Agriculture Across Africa
summary: Improving agricultural productivity while protecting natural resources remains one of Africa s greatest development priorities. Healthy soils, efficient fertilizer use, and sustainable nutrient management are essential for ensuring long-term food security, climate resilience, and increased farmer productivity. To support these goals, the African Plant Nutrition Institute (APNI) has opened applications for the 2026 African Plant Nutrition Outreach Fellowship , an exciting funding opportunity designed to empower agricultural professionals who are committed to transforming plant nutrition education and outreach across the continent. The fellowship provides USD $5,000 awards to outstanding professionals working on innovative education, communication, extension, and outreach initiatives that promote improved soil fertility management and efficient plant nutrient use in African agricultural systems. If you are an agricultural scientist, extension expert, or educator working in Africa and have an innovative idea capable of accelerating the adoption of better nutrient management practices, this fellowship offers both financial support and professional recognition. About the African Plant Nutrition Outreach Fellowship The African Plant Nutrition Outreach Fellowship is an initiative of the African Plant Nutrition Institute (APNI), a non-profit research and education organization established in 2019 and headquartered in Benguérir, Morocco. The institute works to improve plant nutrition throughout Africa by supporting research, innovation, education, and partnerships that strengthen sustainable agricultural systems. Rather than funding conventional research projects alone, this fellowship focuses on helping professionals bridge the gap between scientific knowledge and practical implementation by supporting outreach, education, training, communication, and technology transfer activities that improve nutrient management among farmers and agricultural stakeholders. Successful applicants will receive USD $5,000 to implement creative activities that increase awareness and adoption of improved soil fertility practices. Fellowship Benefits Selected fellows will receive several important benefits, including: Award funding of USD $5,000 Support for innovative agricultural outreach initiatives Opportunity to expand knowledge transfer activities Resources to develop communication materials Funding for educational and training events Support for travel related to outreach activities Recognition from the African Plant Nutrition Institute Opportunity to strengthen collaboration among agricultural stakeholders Contribution toward improving sustainable agriculture across Africa Increased professional visibility within the African agricultural research community Fellowship Objectives The fellowship seeks to accelerate the adoption of improved plant nutrition practices by supporting activities that: Improve farmer education Strengthen agricultural extension services Increase knowledge sharing Promote sustainable fertilizer use Encourage efficient nutrient management Improve soil fertility management Support climate-resilient agriculture Bridge the gap between scientific research and practical implementation Develop innovative communication strategies for agricultural knowledge dissemination APNI Priority Areas Applicants are expected to develop proposals aligned with at least one of APNI s priority initiatives. These include: 1. 4R Nutrient Stewardship Projects promoting the application of nutrients using: Right source Right rate Right time Right place to maximize crop productivity while minimizing environmental impacts. 2. Nutrient and Water Management Innovations for Resilient Agriculture in African Drylands Projects focusing on improving nutrient and water efficiency in drought-prone agricultural systems. 3. Soil Health Nutrient Management and Diagnostics Activities that improve soil testing, nutrient diagnostics, soil health assessment, and better nutrient recommendations. 4. Precision Farming Innovative approaches that utilize technology, data, or precision agriculture methods to improve nutrient use efficiency. 5. Farmer-led On-farm Innovation Projects encouraging farmers to participate directly in testing, adapting, and promoting improved soil fertility management practices. Who Is Eligible? Applications are open to full-time professionals working within Africa. Eligible applicants include: Scientists Agricultural extension specialists Educators Applicants must be employed full-time by one of the following: National Agricultural Research and Extension System (NARES) institutions Universities Non-profit organizations Private sector organizations Students are not eligible for this fellowship. Female applicants are especially encouraged to submit applications. What Makes a Strong Application? APNI is looking for applicants who present creative and practical ideas capable of accelerating the adoption of improved soil fertility management practices across Africa. Competitive applications should demonstrate: Innovation Practical relevance Clear outreach strategy Strong educational value Potential for large-scale impact Effective communication approaches Evidence-based planning Sustainability Collaboration and partnerships Applications showing partnerships with other organizations or institutions will receive favorable consideration. Required Application Documents Applicants must prepare the following documents before beginning the online application process. 1. Detailed Project Description Applicants should explain how the fellowship funding will improve outreach or implementation of soil fertility management. The proposal should clearly describe: New outreach initiatives Communication activities Educational programs Data synthesis Knowledge-sharing activities Training events Planned travel supported by the fellowship Expected impact Innovation Originality The proposal should provide sufficient detail to enable reviewers to evaluate its quality and potential contribution. 2. Two Letters of Support Applicants must upload two signed letters of support. Requirements include: Official institutional letterhead Signature Phone number of the referee Email address of the referee One letter must come from the applicant s supervisor. 3. Resume or Curriculum Vitae (CV) Applicants must submit a CV containing: Academic qualifications Educational background Relevant publications Communication products Professional experience related to soil fertility management 4. Final Report Successful fellows will be required to submit a short report at the conclusion of the fellowship explaining how the funding was used and the outcomes achieved. Language Requirements Applications may be submitted in either: English French Preparing for the Online Application Since documents must be uploaded during the online application process, applicants are encouraged to prepare electronic PDF versions of all required materials before starting the application. Preparing documents in advance can help ensure a smooth submission process. Why Partnerships Matter APNI places significant value on collaborative approaches to agricultural development. Applications demonstrating partnerships with: Universities Research institutions Agricultural organizations Extension services Farmer organizations Private companies Non-governmental organizations may receive favorable consideration during the evaluation process. Why This Fellowship Matters Africa faces increasing challenges related to soil degradation, declining fertility, climate change, and food insecurity. Improving plant nutrient management is one of the most effective strategies for increasing crop yields while protecting environmental resources. By investing in scientists, educators, and extension professionals, the African Plant Nutrition Outreach Fellowship aims to accelerate the adoption of practical, science-based agricultural solutions that can directly benefit farming communities throughout Africa. The fellowship supports not only innovation but also the effective communication of research findings, ensuring that scientific knowledge reaches those who need it most. Visit here for more details on 2026 African Plant Nutrition Outreach Fellowship Application Deadline Applicants must submit their applications by September 21, 2026 . Late submissions may not be considered, so interested candidates are encouraged to prepare all required documents and complete the online application well before the deadline. Apply here About the African Plant Nutrition Institute (APNI) The African Plant Nutrition Institute (APNI) is a not-for-profit research and education organization founded in 2019 and headquartered in Benguérir, Morocco. Its mission is to enhance plant nutrition across Africa in order to build resilient agricultural systems and improve food security. title: Japan Africa Dream Scholarship (JADS) 2026: Fully Funded Master’s Scholarship for African Students
summary: The Japan Africa Dream Scholarship (JADS) is now accepting applications from outstanding African students seeking to pursue fully funded Master s degree studies in fields that are critical to Africa s sustainable development. Jointly established by the African Development Bank (AfDB) and the Government of Japan , the scholarship aims to strengthen Africa s human resource capacity by equipping future leaders with advanced knowledge and technical skills needed to accelerate development across the continent. The scholarship provides exceptional students from eligible African countries with the opportunity to undertake postgraduate studies at selected partner universities while receiving comprehensive financial support throughout their academic journey. Graduates are expected to return to their home countries after completing their studies to apply their newly acquired expertise toward advancing national and continental development priorities. About the Japan Africa Dream Scholarship (JADS) The Japan Africa Dream Scholarship (JADS) is a capacity-building initiative designed to support Africa s long-term development by investing in talented professionals who demonstrate strong academic achievement and a commitment to public service and development. The programme aligns with the African Development Bank s High 5 Strategic Priorities , which include: Feed Africa Light Up and Power Africa Industrialize Africa Integrate Africa Improve the Quality of Life for the People of Africa These priorities also complement Japan s international development cooperation initiatives aimed at promoting sustainable economic growth and human capital development across Africa. Fields of Study The scholarship supports Master s degree programmes in development-focused disciplines, including: Energy Agriculture Health Environmental Sustainability Engineering These fields have been carefully selected to address Africa s most pressing development challenges while contributing to innovation, economic growth, and sustainable transformation. Scholarship Benefits The Japan Africa Dream Scholarship provides comprehensive financial support to successful applicants throughout the duration of their Master s programme. The scholarship covers: Tuition Fees Recipients receive full tuition fee coverage for up to 24 months , covering the entire duration of the eligible graduate programme. Monthly Living Allowance Scholars receive a monthly stipend throughout their studies to help cover living expenses. International Airfare The scholarship finances: One economy-class ticket from the scholar s home country to the host university at the beginning of the programme. One return economy-class ticket upon successful completion of the scholarship. Health Insurance Health insurance is provided, typically through the host university. Additional Study or Internship Support The scholarship may also provide an additional six months of support for: Preparatory academic study Professional internships after graduation Research Support Students undertaking research projects may receive additional funding for: Research activities Thesis preparation Additional Preparatory Courses Where necessary, the scholarship may also cover: Computer literacy courses Preparatory language programmes Similar academic preparation required by the programme What the Scholarship Does Not Cover Applicants should note that certain expenses are not included under the scholarship. These include: Costs associated with accompanying or supporting family members. Extracurricular courses or training. Language courses that are not part of the graduate programme. Supplementary educational materials. Field trips. Conference or seminar participation. Computers and other educational equipment. Applicants should carefully consider these additional costs when planning their studies. Important Funding Policy The Japan Africa Dream Scholarship is intended to complement—not duplicate—other financial support. If applicants are selected as scholarship finalists or awardees, they must disclose any additional scholarships, fellowships, or financial assistance they receive. Failure to disclose additional funding may result in the reduction or withdrawal of the JADS scholarship. Application Process Unlike many scholarship programmes, applicants do not submit a separate scholarship application directly to the African Development Bank. Instead, applications follow a university-based selection process. The process includes: Identify a participating JADS partner university. Contact the university to request admission information and application procedures. Submit an application for admission to the selected university. The university evaluates applications and issues provisional admission offers to successful candidates. The university nominates selected candidates to the African Development Bank. The African Development Bank, together with the JADS Programme Implementation Unit (PIU), evaluates nominated applicants. Successful scholarship recipients are notified by the African Development Bank. Only candidates who have been admitted to a participating JADS partner university and formally endorsed by that university will be considered for the scholarship. How to Prepare a Strong Application Prospective applicants are encouraged to begin preparing early. Recommended preparation includes: Carefully reviewing the eligibility criteria. Preparing an updated Curriculum Vitae (CV). Collecting proof of employment covering all employment since completing a Bachelor s degree. Obtaining certified copies of academic certificates. Identifying two professional referees. Preparing a strong research proposal or research plan where required. Completing English language proficiency examinations such as TOEFL iBT or TOEIC if required by the chosen university. Preparing these documents in advance can significantly improve the application process. Important Information for Applicants Applicants should note several important conditions: Applications must be submitted through participating JADS partner universities. No separate application should be submitted directly to the African Development Bank. Admission to a JADS partner university does not automatically guarantee scholarship funding. Applicants should not resign from employment or make major commitments until they receive official scholarship confirmation from the African Development Bank. Following these guidelines carefully is essential to ensure a successful application. For More Information Prospective applicants should contact their chosen JADS partner university to obtain detailed admission procedures, scholarship application requirements, and programme-specific guidance. Additional information about eligibility, participating universities, and the scholarship programme is available on the official Japan Africa Dream Scholarship (JADS) website and through the African Development Bank . Applicants are encouraged to communicate directly with their selected university regarding admission timelines and documentation requirements before beginning the application process. Conclusion The Japan Africa Dream Scholarship (JADS) offers an exceptional opportunity for talented African students to pursue fully funded Master s degree studies in fields that are central to Africa s future development. Through generous financial support, world-class education, and strong institutional partnerships between the African Development Bank and the Government of Japan, the programme prepares the next generation of African leaders to address critical development challenges. Interested applicants are encouraged to review the eligibility requirements carefully, secure admission to a participating partner university, and begin preparing the necessary application documents early to maximize their chances of success. title: Compass Civics Youth Policy Research Program Fall 2026: Apply to Build Policy Research Skills, Influence Decision-Makers, and Drive Community Change
summary: The Compass Civics Youth Policy Research Program is now accepting applications for Fall 2026 , offering an exciting opportunity for young civic leaders to strengthen their policy research skills while making meaningful contributions to their communities. This mentorship-driven program is designed to help participants understand the policy-making process, develop evidence-based solutions to real-world issues, and present their recommendations directly to community leaders and decision-makers. For young people who are passionate about creating positive social change, influencing public policy, and becoming future civic leaders, the Compass Civics Youth Policy Research Program provides an ideal platform to transform ideas into practical policy solutions. What is the Compass Civics Youth Policy Research Program? The Compass Civics Youth Policy Research Program is a structured educational initiative that equips youth with the knowledge and practical skills needed to participate effectively in public policy development. Unlike traditional academic research projects, this program focuses on solving real community challenges through evidence-based research and policy analysis. Participants work through each stage of the policy development process—from identifying an issue to proposing practical solutions—and ultimately present their findings to local leaders. The program combines mentorship, research, communication training, and civic engagement into one comprehensive learning experience that prepares participants to become informed and active contributors to their communities. Program Objectives The primary goal of the program is to empower young people to engage thoughtfully and effectively in civic life by helping them understand how public policies are created, evaluated, and improved. Participants learn how to: Identify pressing community issues. Conduct evidence-based research. Evaluate existing policies and legislation. Develop practical policy recommendations. Communicate ideas professionally. Present policy proposals to decision-makers. Strengthen civic leadership skills. Skills Participants Will Gain Throughout the program, students develop a wide range of transferable skills that are valuable for future academic studies, leadership opportunities, and professional careers. These include: Research Skills Participants learn how to: Conduct evidence-based research. Gather reliable information. Analyze data and community needs. Evaluate multiple information sources. Develop informed conclusions. Critical Thinking Students strengthen their ability to: Examine complex public issues. Evaluate policy effectiveness. Identify gaps in existing systems. Step 2: Analyze Policy Options After researching the issue, participants evaluate current laws, policies, and approaches that address the problem. During this stage, they: Examine existing legislation. Review policy effectiveness. Identify policy gaps. Compare alternative approaches. Develop improved policy recommendations. This process encourages analytical thinking and practical problem-solving. Step 3: Create a Professional Policy Brief Students then prepare a professional-quality policy brief that clearly communicates: The identified problem. Supporting research. Policy analysis. Recommended solutions. Expected outcomes. In addition to the written document, participants also create a concise presentation summarizing their findings. Step 4: Present Your Policy Solution One of the most valuable aspects of the program is the opportunity to present policy recommendations directly to community leaders and decision-makers. Participants share their research and proposed solutions while gaining firsthand experience in civic participation and public engagement. This real-world presentation experience helps students build confidence while understanding how research can influence policy discussions. Why Join the Compass Civics Youth Policy Research Program? The program offers several benefits for aspiring civic leaders, including: Hands-on policy research experience. Mentorship throughout the research process. Development of professional research and communication skills. Opportunities to solve real community challenges. Experience preparing policy briefs. Public speaking and presentation practice. Direct engagement with community leaders. Strong preparation for future academic and leadership opportunities. Improved understanding of government and public policy. Who Should Apply? The program is particularly suitable for: Youth interested in civic leadership. Students passionate about public policy. Future lawyers and political science students. Community advocates. Young researchers. Aspiring public servants. Individuals interested in social impact and community development. Applicants who enjoy research, problem-solving, leadership, and creating meaningful change within their communities will benefit significantly from this opportunity. Prospective applicants are encouraged to review the program requirements and submit their applications before the official closing date once announced. Application Deadline 1st August,2026. Conclusion The Compass Civics Youth Policy Research Program provides an outstanding opportunity for young civic leaders to move beyond classroom learning and actively contribute to solving real community challenges. Through mentorship, evidence-based research, policy analysis, and direct engagement with community leaders, participants develop practical skills that extend far beyond the duration of the program. Whether you aspire to work in public policy, law, government, advocacy, or community leadership, this program offers a valuable foundation for future success. By participating, students gain the confidence, knowledge, and experience needed to influence meaningful change while becoming informed and engaged citizens. If you are passionate about improving your community through research and policy innovation, the Fall 2026 Compass Civics Youth Policy Research Program is an opportunity worth exploring. title: Newnham College Research Fellowships 2027: Fully Funded Research Opportunities for Outstanding Female Early-Career Researchers Worldwide
summary: Applications are now open for the prestigious Newnham College Research Fellowships 2027 at the University of Cambridge , offering exceptional early-career female researchers from around the world the opportunity to pursue independent research within one of the world s leading academic institutions. Designed to support women at the beginning of their academic careers, these highly competitive fellowships provide generous financial support, research funding, access to an internationally renowned scholarly community, and the freedom to focus exclusively on research for up to three years. The fellowship programme is open to eligible female researchers from any country and spans a broad range of disciplines, including Science, Mathematics, Engineering, Psychology, Arts, Humanities, and Social Sciences. If you are an outstanding researcher seeking to advance your academic career at one of the most prestigious universities in the world, this fellowship offers an exceptional platform to develop your research while collaborating with leading scholars across disciplines. About the Newnham College Research Fellowships Newnham College, one of the constituent colleges of the University of Cambridge, has a long-standing commitment to supporting women in higher education and research. Through its Research Fellowship programme, the College provides early-career researchers with the opportunity to establish themselves as independent scholars in a stimulating and supportive academic environment. Research Fellows become part of Newnham College s vibrant scholarly community, where they can engage with academics across diverse disciplines, collaborate with fellow researchers, and participate in the intellectual life of the College. Unlike many academic positions, these fellowships are designed to allow fellows to concentrate primarily on their own research without significant teaching or administrative responsibilities. Research Fellowship Opportunities Available Newnham College currently offers several prestigious research fellowship schemes, including: Junior Research Fellowships (JRF) Early Career Fellowship in Engineering Engineering Research Fellowship Margaret Anstee Research Fellowships Applications are currently invited for selected fellowship schemes, while others will be advertised separately through Newnham College s vacancies page. Junior Research Fellowships The Junior Research Fellowships are intended to support outstanding women researchers during the early stages of their academic careers. These fellowships provide recipients with the time, resources, and academic environment necessary to establish themselves as leading researchers while building strong foundations for future academic appointments. The fellowships are highly competitive and attract applications from exceptional researchers worldwide. Fellowship Duration Successful applicants will normally be appointed for: Three years Although the fellowship runs for three years, some fellows may leave earlier if they secure permanent academic positions at Cambridge or other institutions. Financial Support Successful fellows receive an attractive financial package that includes: A stipend at Point 42 on the University of Cambridge salary scale , valued at £38,784 (2025–26 rate, subject to future pay adjustments) . Annual salary progression over a three-point scale. Potential access to College accommodation available for rent. Research funding to support conference participation and research activities. A one-time allocation of up to £10,000 to organize an approved Newnham-based academic event such as: Conferences Workshops Seminar series These benefits are intended to provide fellows with both financial stability and opportunities to develop their academic networks. Research Environment One of the defining features of the Newnham College Research Fellowships is the opportunity to conduct independent research within one of the world s leading universities. Research Fellows benefit from: A supportive interdisciplinary academic community. Opportunities to collaborate with established researchers. Access to University of Cambridge facilities and resources. Participation in College seminars and academic events. Membership of the College Governing Body. Opportunities to serve on College committees. Although fellows are not required to undertake teaching, they may choose to participate in limited College activities such as: Small-scale teaching. Mentoring postgraduate students. Admissions interviewing. Student pastoral support. Newnham College will next invite applications in: August 2027 The successful fellow will commence the fellowship on: 1 October 2028 Eligibility Requirements Applicants should note that these fellowships are designed specifically to support women at an early stage of their academic careers. Eligible applicants should: Have recently completed a PhD. Have recently submitted a PhD thesis. Have no more than a few years of full-time postdoctoral research experience. title: ATCMA-ECCAS Call for Expressions of Interest 2026: EU-Funded Opportunity for Timber, Cocoa, and Cassava SMEs in Central Africa
summary: The Programme for Trade Competitiveness and Market Access in Central Africa (ATCMA-ECCAS) has officially launched a Call for Expressions of Interest inviting eligible small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) operating in the timber, cocoa, and cassava value chains to apply for comprehensive technical support aimed at improving competitiveness, increasing productivity, enhancing product quality, and expanding access to regional, continental, and international markets. Funded by the European Union (EU) and jointly implemented by the International Trade Centre (ITC) and the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) , the programme seeks to strengthen private sector development across Central Africa by helping businesses modernize their operations, adopt sustainable production practices, comply with international quality standards, and unlock new trade and export opportunities. For SMEs seeking to scale their businesses, improve production systems, or enter new markets, this initiative presents a valuable opportunity to receive expert technical assistance without direct financial cost while becoming more competitive in an increasingly global marketplace. About the ATCMA-ECCAS Programme The Programme for Trade Competitiveness and Market Access in Central Africa (ATCMA-ECCAS) is a regional initiative established to improve the competitiveness of businesses throughout the Economic Community of Central African States (ECCAS). The programme recognizes that many SMEs possess significant production potential but face numerous challenges that limit their ability to compete in both domestic and international markets. These challenges often include outdated production methods, limited value addition, inadequate quality assurance systems, insufficient certification, poor access to export markets, and limited technical capacity. Through targeted technical assistance, the programme aims to help enterprises overcome these barriers while contributing to sustainable economic growth, regional integration, industrial development, and increased trade throughout Central Africa. The initiative is financed by the European Union and implemented through a partnership between two internationally recognized organizations: International Trade Centre (ITC) United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) Together, these organizations provide technical expertise, business development support, and capacity-building services designed to strengthen participating enterprises. Objective of the Call for Expressions of Interest The primary objective of this Call for Expressions of Interest is to identify promising SMEs that are ready to improve their competitiveness and expand their commercial activities. Rather than providing direct financial grants, the programme focuses on delivering specialized technical support that enables businesses to become more efficient, productive, sustainable, and export-ready. Selected companies will receive customized support that addresses their individual business needs while positioning them for long-term growth. Priority Value Chains This call specifically targets enterprises operating within three strategic agricultural and industrial value chains: 1. Timber Eligible timber enterprises may include businesses involved in: Wood processing Timber transformation Furniture manufacturing Timber product value addition Sustainable forestry production Wood exports 2. Cocoa The programme welcomes cocoa enterprises involved in: Cocoa production Cocoa processing Chocolate manufacturing Cocoa value addition Packaging Export development 3. Cassava Cassava businesses operating in areas such as: Cassava processing Food manufacturing Industrial cassava products Value-added cassava products Commercial production Export-oriented activities are encouraged to apply. Programme Areas of Support The ATCMA-ECCAS programme focuses on strengthening businesses across several important areas. 1. Local Processing and Product Upgrading Participating enterprises will receive support to: Improve processing techniques. Increase product value. Diversify product offerings. Produce higher-quality finished products. Reduce post-harvest losses. Improved local processing helps businesses capture more value before products enter domestic or export markets. 2. Strengthening Productive and Commercial Capacity The programme helps SMEs become stronger businesses by supporting: Improved production efficiency. Better operational management. Increased productivity. Business planning. Market positioning. Commercial growth. 3. Improving Quality Standards and Certification Meeting international standards is essential for accessing high-value export markets. The programme supports businesses through: Quality management improvements. Compliance with international standards. Certification support. Product traceability. Food safety systems where applicable. Sustainable production standards. 4. Regional and International Market Integration Selected enterprises will receive guidance to access: National markets. Regional markets. Continental markets. International export opportunities. The programme encourages businesses to become competitive suppliers capable of meeting international buyer requirements. 5. Sustainable Business Practices Modern markets increasingly demand sustainability. The programme promotes: Environmentally responsible production. Sustainable sourcing. Resource efficiency. Responsible manufacturing. Competitive green business practices. 6. Trade and Export Development Businesses will also receive assistance to: Expand exports. Identify buyers. Improve market access. Participate in trade promotion activities. Strengthen commercial relationships. Technical Support Available Selected companies will benefit from a comprehensive package of technical assistance tailored to their business needs. Support may include the following. Company Diagnostics Experts will conduct detailed assessments of participating enterprises to identify strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and priority improvement areas. Development of Upgrading Plans Each company may receive a customized upgrading roadmap outlining practical actions needed to improve competitiveness and business performance. Modernization Support The programme assists enterprises in modernizing operations through: Improved production methods. Technology adoption. Operational improvements. Increased efficiency. Digitalisation Support Businesses will receive assistance in integrating digital tools that enhance productivity, management, marketing, and commercial operations. Production Process Improvement Experts will help companies optimize production systems to improve quality, efficiency, and consistency. Technical Training Participants will benefit from specialized training covering: Production techniques. Business management. Export readiness. Product quality. Sustainable practices. Coaching and Mentorship Businesses will receive personalized coaching from experienced experts who will provide guidance throughout the improvement process. Quality and Certification Support Technical experts will help companies: Improve product quality. Prepare for certification. Strengthen traceability systems. Meet export compliance requirements. Sustainable Production Practices The programme encourages adoption of sustainable production methods that improve competitiveness while protecting environmental resources. Commercial Development Businesses will receive support in: Business expansion. Market development. Sales improvement. Customer acquisition. Export Development Participating enterprises will be assisted in preparing for international trade through export readiness support. Trade Fairs and Business Meetings Selected companies may receive support to participate in: Trade fairs. International exhibitions. Business matchmaking events. Commercial networking opportunities. These activities provide valuable exposure to potential buyers, investors, and commercial partners. Eligibility Requirements To qualify for this Call for Expressions of Interest, applicants must satisfy all four of the following conditions. 1. Legal Registration The business must be legally registered within an ECCAS Member State. 2. Operate in Eligible Value Chains The company must operate within one of the following sectors: Timber Cocoa Cassava 3. Active Business Operations Only companies that are currently operational and actively conducting business are eligible. 4. Commitment to Growth Applicants should demonstrate a clear intention to: Improve competitiveness. Expand commercial activities. Strengthen production capacity. Develop export opportunities. The programme will verify compliance with these requirements using information provided in the application questionnaire and supporting documentation. Application Process Interested companies must complete the official Expression of Interest questionnaire. Estimated Completion Time Approximately 15 minutes . Applicants should ensure that all submitted information is accurate, complete, and supported by the required documentation. Data Confidentiality All information submitted through the application process will be handled confidentially. The collected information will be used exclusively for: Selecting beneficiary companies. Implementing programme activities. Monitoring programme implementation. Programme evaluation. By submitting an application, each company confirms that: The information provided is accurate. The information is complete. It agrees to data processing for programme implementation. It will actively participate in programme activities if selected. It will cooperate with programme experts during diagnostics and implementation. Contact Information Applicants with questions regarding this Call for Expressions of Interest may contact the programme team through the following email addresses: DWANDJI@intracen.org S.MEVONOANGON@unido.org hbangda@intracen.org Important Deadline Application Deadline: 21 August 2026 Applicants are encouraged to complete and submit their applications well before the closing date to avoid last-minute technical issues or incomplete submissions. APPLY HERE Why Businesses Should Apply Participation in the ATCMA-ECCAS programme offers SMEs a unique opportunity to receive expert technical assistance that can transform their operations and improve their long-term competitiveness. Key advantages include: Access to international technical expertise. Business diagnostics and tailored upgrading plans. Improved production systems. Enhanced product quality. Support for certification and compliance. Export readiness assistance. Commercial development support. Participation in trade fairs and business events. Increased competitiveness in regional and global markets. Adoption of sustainable and modern business practices. Rather than providing one-time financial assistance, the programme focuses on building lasting business capacity that enables enterprises to grow sustainably over the long term. Visit HERE for more information about the ATCMA-ECCAS Call for Expressions of Interest 2026. Conclusion The ATCMA-ECCAS Call for Expressions of Interest is an outstanding opportunity for SMEs operating in the timber, cocoa, and cassava value chains across Central Africa to strengthen their businesses and expand into new markets. Through the combined expertise of the European Union, the International Trade Centre, and the United Nations Industrial Development Organization, selected enterprises will receive tailored technical support aimed at improving productivity, quality, sustainability, and export readiness. Businesses that meet the eligibility requirements should take advantage of this opportunity by submitting their applications before the 21 August 2026 deadline and positioning themselves for sustainable commercial growth in regional and international markets.
