title: Free UN Sustainable Finance Courses with Digital Certificates: Learn Sustainable Finance, Green Finance, SDG Financing, and Sustainable Finance Taxonomies
summary: As the world accelerates efforts to combat climate change and achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), sustainable finance has become one of the most important areas of knowledge for policymakers, financial professionals, businesses, researchers, students, and development practitioners. Financial institutions and governments across the globe are increasingly integrating sustainability into investment decisions, banking, insurance, lending, and economic policies. To help build global capacity in this rapidly growing field, UN CC:Learn offers a collection of self-paced online courses that provide participants with practical and technical knowledge on sustainable finance. These courses are designed by leading international organizations and financial institutions and provide learners with the opportunity to earn an official UN digital certificate upon successful completion. Among the most valuable learning opportunities currently available are: Introduction to Sustainable Finance Introduction to Sustainable Finance Taxonomies SDG Learncast Microlearning: Global Finance in Transition – Reforming the Global Financial System for the SDGs These learning opportunities are suitable for professionals seeking to strengthen their understanding of sustainable development financing, green finance instruments, climate finance, financial regulations, and the transformation of global financial systems. Why Sustainable Finance Matters Sustainable finance refers to financial activities that integrate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) considerations into investment and financial decision-making. Rather than focusing solely on short-term financial returns, sustainable finance promotes investments that contribute to: Climate change mitigation Climate adaptation Environmental protection Social inclusion Responsible governance Long-term economic growth Achievement of the UN Sustainable Development Goals Implementation of the Paris Agreement on Climate Change Governments, banks, investment firms, insurance companies, regulators, development organizations, and businesses are increasingly adopting sustainable finance principles to ensure that financial resources contribute to a more resilient and inclusive global economy. The UN CC:Learn courses provide participants with foundational and practical knowledge needed to understand this evolving field. Course 1: Introduction to Sustainable Finance Course Overview The Introduction to Sustainable Finance course is an interactive, self-paced online programme that provides comprehensive technical knowledge about the contribution of sustainable finance to sustainable development. Originally developed in 2018 and extensively updated in 2021, the course combines theory with practical examples, enabling participants to understand how sustainability considerations can be integrated into financial systems and policy frameworks. Course Information Learning mode: Self-paced Duration: Approximately 10 hours Language: English Certificate available Digital certification fee: USD 20 Platform: UN CC:Learn Learning Objectives Participants will gain the ability to: Understand how sustainable finance supports the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Explain how sustainable finance contributes to implementing the Paris Climate Agreement. Understand the core principles of sustainable finance. Identify sustainability risks and opportunities within financial systems. Learn how governments and regulators shape sustainable finance. Explore major sustainable finance products. Understand sustainable finance regulations and industry initiatives. Learn how financial institutions integrate sustainability into investment decisions. Course Modules The programme consists of four comprehensive modules. Module 1: Sustainable Finance in Context This introductory module explores: Global climate challenges Sustainable development priorities The relationship between finance and sustainable development The role of finance in achieving international environmental goals Module 2: Fundamentals of Sustainable Finance This module introduces the basic concepts of sustainable finance, including: ESG considerations Financial decision-making Sustainable investment approaches Sustainability risk management Financial sector responsibilities Module 3: Sustainable Finance Regulation and Self-Regulation Participants explore: Government regulations Financial sector standards Industry initiatives Voluntary sustainability frameworks Regulatory developments around the world Module 4: Sustainable Finance Products Learners discover major financial products that support sustainable development, including: Green bonds Sustainability bonds Social bonds Green loans Sustainability-linked loans Climate finance instruments UN Digital Certificate Participants who score at least 70% on all quizzes become eligible for a UN Digital Certificate. Important requirements include: Minimum passing score: 70% Maximum of three attempts per quiz Certificate issued after payment of USD 20 Certificate can be downloaded and shared digitally The digital certificate provides internationally recognized evidence of successful completion. Course Partners The course was developed through collaboration between internationally recognized organizations including: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) Skandinaviska Enskilda Banken (SEB) Partnership for Action on Green Economy (PAGE) German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) United Nations Environment Programme Finance Initiative (UNEP FI) These organizations collectively contribute extensive expertise in sustainable finance, green bond markets, climate finance, and international development. APPLY HERE Visit HERE to learn more about the Introduction to Sustainable Finance. Course 2: Introduction to Sustainable Finance Taxonomies Course Overview The Introduction to Sustainable Finance Taxonomies course focuses on one of the fastest-growing areas of sustainable finance: sustainable finance taxonomies. Taxonomies help governments, investors, regulators, and businesses classify economic activities according to sustainability criteria, making it easier to direct investments toward environmentally and socially responsible activities. The course combines practical case studies with technical guidance to help participants understand how taxonomies are designed and implemented.
